title: The Army is preparing to test robotic Ford F-250 pickup trucks
excerpt: The Army is preparing to test autonomous Ford F-250 pickup trucks in a training exercise to see if they can perform dangerous battlefield jobs.
content_html:
The US Army is preparing to test autonomous Ford F-250 pickup trucks in a training exercise, part of a broader effort to determine whether familiar commercial vehicles can perform dangerous battlefield jobs without soldiers.

Forterra, the defense-technology company supplying the trucks' autonomous-driving system, says that the vehicles could eventually support missions such as route clearance and breaching, work that can require soldiers to spend hours searching mined roads and positioning explosives.

The Army's XVIII Airborne Corps plans to experiment with four Forterra-equipped F-250s.

Ford's popularity and readily available supply of parts could make the robotic trucks easier to maintain and repair, said Pat Acox, Forterra's vice president of defense.

For many military systems, the Pentagon has notoriously complex supply chains for thousands of specialized parts available from only a small number of manufacturers, or in some cases, sole suppliers.

Spare part availability and delivery delays have been known to sideline military equipment for months, even years, and have contributed to equipment readiness problems.

Forterra's autonomous software is already being integrated into the Marine Corps' Navy-Marine Expeditionary Ship Interdiction System (NMESIS), an anti-ship missile system built on the chassis of the Joint Light Tactical Vehicle.

The company has also delivered over 100 smaller, ruggedized vehicles to Ukraine that are already performing ground missions, Acox said. Those vehicles come complete with a Starlink internet antenna and can haul heavy loads up to nearly 1700 pounds.

Uncrewed ground vehicles are increasingly prolific in Ukraine, where they've been used to varying degrees of effectiveness for missions like assaults and casualty evacuation, reducing the risks to the troops facing constant threats from small aerial drones, particularly in front-line kill zones.

The battlefield in Ukraine has also exposed some limitations with remotely operated vehicles. Video feeds require significant bandwidth and can generate an electronic warfare signature that enemy forces might detect, Acox said.

Rather than being continuously driven by distant operators, vehicles can instead receive short, low-bandwidth commands similar to text messages or follow pre-programmed routes.

The Pentagon sees autonomous vehicles as a way to remove troops from dangerous, time-consuming work while freeing them for other missions, but systems have to be rugged and reliable enough to effectively take on human tasks in combat.

content_html_zh:
美国陆军正准备在一次训练演习中测试自动福特 F-250 皮卡，这是更广泛努力的一部分，旨在确定熟悉的商用车辆是否可以在没有士兵的情况下执行危险的战场工作。

提供卡车自动驾驶系统的国防技术公司 Forterra 表示，这些车辆最终可以支持诸如路线清理和突破等任务，这些任务可能需要士兵花费数小时搜索埋有地雷的道路并放置炸药。

陆军第十八空降军计划试验四架配备 Forterra 的 F-250。

Forterra 国防副总裁帕特·阿科克斯 (Pat Acox) 表示，福特的受欢迎程度和随时可用的零部件供应可以使机器人卡车更容易维护和修理。

对于许多军事系统来说，五角大楼拥有极其复杂的供应链，其中数千种专用零件仅由少数制造商提供，或者在某些情况下由唯一供应商提供。

众所周知，备件供应和交付延迟会导致军事装备停产数月甚至数年，并导致装备准备问题。

Forterra的自主软件已经被集成到海军陆战队的海军-海军陆战队远征舰拦截系统（NMESIS）中，这是一种建立在联合轻型战术车辆底盘上的反舰导弹系统。

Acox 表示，该公司还向乌克兰交付了 100 多辆小型、坚固的车辆，这些车辆已经在执行地面任务。 这些车辆配备了 Starlink 互联网天线，可以牵引近 1700 磅的重物。

无人驾驶地面车辆在乌克兰越来越多，它们被不同程度地用于执行攻击和伤员疏散等任务，降低了部队面临小型无人机持续威胁的风险，特别是在前线杀伤区。

乌克兰战场也暴露出遥控车辆的一些局限性。 阿科克斯说，视频源需要大量带宽，并且可以生成敌军可能检测到的电子战信号。

车辆不再需要由远处的操作员持续驾驶，而是可以接收类似于短信的简短、低带宽命令或遵循预先编程的路线。

五角大楼将自动驾驶车辆视为一种将部队从危险、耗时的工作中解放出来，同时将他们解放出来执行其他任务的方法，但系统必须足够坚固和可靠，才能在战斗中有效地承担人类任务。
